sections.title: Portfolio & Leverage
sections.subtitle: EPRA-standard REIT metrics: NAV, leverage, occupancy and rent growth

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Vonovia SE: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Vonovia SE: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Vonovia SE: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Vonovia SE: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Vonovia SE: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Vonovia SE: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

epraNta.title: EPRA NTA (Net Tangible Assets)
epraNta.content:
EPRA NTA is the EPRA-standard net asset value for a long-term buy-and-hold property investor: net assets adjusted to exclude the mark-to-market of fixed-rate debt and deferred tax on revaluations that would not actually be paid if the portfolio is held rather than sold.

For Vonovia SE: this is the NAV the market discounts when it prices the shares below book -- German residential landlords have traded at a persistent discount to EPRA NTA since the 2022 rate shock repriced the whole sector's cost of debt.

What to watch:

  • EPRA NTA growth from rent-driven cap-rate stability versus pure revaluation swings
  • Share price discount/premium to EPRA NTA per share

ltv.title: Loan-to-Value (LTV)
ltv.content:
LTV is net debt divided by the fair value of the investment property portfolio -- the core leverage covenant metric for a REIT, distinct from net-debt/EBITDA used elsewhere.

For Vonovia SE: management targets LTV in the mid-40s%; it rose into the high-40s during the 2022-2023 property devaluation (fair value fell while debt did not) and has been brought back down since via disposals and the portfolio's value recovery.

What to watch:

  • LTV rising from falling property values rather than rising debt
  • Distance from rating-agency and bond-covenant LTV thresholds

vacancyRate.title: Vacancy rate
vacancyRate.content:
The percentage of residential units in the owned portfolio standing empty at period end.

For Vonovia SE: structurally low (around 2%) because German residential demand in Vonovia's core cities persistently exceeds supply -- this is the occupancy side of the rent-growth story, not a demand-risk indicator the way it would be for a commercial landlord.

What to watch:

  • A rise from the ~2% baseline would signal a genuine demand shift
  • Read alongside in-place rent: low vacancy plus rising rent is pricing power

portfolioValue.title: Portfolio fair value
portfolioValue.content:
The fair value of Vonovia's investment property portfolio under IAS 40, reassessed at each balance-sheet date by external appraisers.

For Vonovia SE: this is the denominator in LTV and the main driver of EPRA NTA; it roughly doubled 2020-2021 (Deutsche Wohnen merger plus a hot cap-rate environment) then fell for two straight years as 2022's rate shock repriced cap rates across German residential before stabilising.

What to watch:

  • Cap-rate assumptions driving valuation more than rent growth
  • Fair-value moves versus actual transaction evidence (disposals)

rentGrowth.title: Organic rent growth and in-place rent
rentGrowth.content:
Organic rent growth is the like-for-like increase in rent on the existing portfolio (new leases plus modernisation plus index/reference-rent effects), excluding acquisitions. In-place rent is the average contracted rent per square metre per month.

For Vonovia SE: German rent-control rules (Mietpreisbremse, reference-rent indices) cap how fast in-place rent can catch up to market rent, so organic growth here is a regulated, low-single-digit number rather than a market-driven one.

What to watch:

  • Organic growth trend against regulatory caps and modernisation surcharge rules
  • In-place rent versus new-letting rent (the uncaptured upside)

units.title: Units owned and managed
units.content:
Units owned is apartments Vonovia holds on its own balance sheet; units managed adds third-party units it administers for a fee (joint ventures, outside owners) via its property-management business.

For Vonovia SE: owned units have declined since the FY2021 Deutsche Wohnen merger peak as disposals (South Portfolio deals, etc.) deleveraged the balance sheet, while the managed book is a separate fee-income stream not reflected in GrossRentalIncome.

What to watch:

  • Owned-unit count falling faster than rental income (asset-light shift via disposals)
  • Managed units as a growing fee business distinct from the owned portfolio

nta.title: NTA per share
nta.content:
NTA per share is net tangible assets divided by shares -- the book value of the portfolio.

For Vonovia SE: the share price relative to NTA is the market's view of the portfolio's valuation and management.

What to watch:

  • Discount or premium to NTA
  • NTA growth from revaluations versus retained cash

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Vonovia SE: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Vonovia SE: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

rental.title: Gross rental income
rental.content:
Rent received from tenants before property expenses.

For Vonovia SE: compare with AFFO to see how much of rent reaches owners.

What to watch:

  • Like-for-like rental growth

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Vonovia SE: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Vonovia SE: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
